findings.title: Unknown/incompatible BIM↔CWICR units convert at 1.0; estimate_from_qto forces m³ → 1000× cost overbill
findings.description: BIMCostEstimator.estimate_element converts QTO quantity into the CWICR match unit via _convert_units, then multiplies by unit_price into official Excel totals. _convert_units returns conversions.get(key, 1.0) for any pair outside six entries (mm→m, m³→m², ASCII aliases). estimate_from_qto (Quick Start estimate_from_bim_model) hardcodes quantity_unit="m³" for every category. Distinct from already-reported prompt injection and project_name path traversal on this same skill, and from the separate cwicr-quantity-matcher skill.
findings.impact: Official BIM cost Estimate.xlsx overbills: 12 m pipe at $65/m becomes $780,000 when exported as 12000 mm. GMP/bid/pay-app baselines follow that total.
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator deploys estimate_from_qto / estimate_element / estimate_from_bim_model.
2. Attacker or Revit QTO supplies mm (or other unknown/incompatible units); estimate_from_qto also forces m³.
3. _convert_units misses → factor 1.0; adjusted_qty stays raw.
4. generate_estimate_report writes Total = qty × CWICR unit_price.
findings.remediation: Fail closed on unknown/incompatible units. Add mm↔m. Map QTO column/category to unit instead of hardcoding m³. Do not emit Total Cost without a real conversion.
findings.poc_video_notes: Video not feasible — SKILL.md template. PoC: 12m@$65=$780; 12000mm@$65=$780000; ft²→m² still converts.
